AbstractText.Label: Background and Aims
AbstractText.content: Preliminary evidence suggests fermentable carbohydrate restriction might ameliorate functional gastrointestinal symptoms (FGS) in quiescent inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Our aim was to determine whether fermentable carbohydrates exacerbate FGS in quiescent IBD using a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, cross-over, re-challenge trial.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: Patients with quiescent IBD and FGS responsive to a low FODMAP diet were allocated to a series of 3-day fermentable carbohydrate challenges in random order (fructan, 12 g/d; galacto-oligosaccharides, GOS, 6 g/d; sorbitol, 6 g/d; and glucose placebo, 12 g/d), each separated by a standardised washout period. Symptoms and stool output were measured daily during the challenges.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: Thirty-two patients with IBD, fulfilling the criteria for irritable bowel syndrome, functional bloating or functional diarrhoea, were recruited and data were available for 29 patients completing all arms of the trial (12 Crohn's, 17 ulcerative colitis). Significantly fewer patients reported adequate relief of FGS on the final day day of the fructan challenge (18/29, 62.1%) compared to glucose (26/29, 89.7%) (p=0.033). There was significantly greater severity of pain (1.1 vs. 0.5, P=0.004), bloating (1.3 vs. 0.6, P=0.002), flatulence (1.5 vs. 0.7, P=0.004) and faecal urgency (0.9 vs. 0.4, P=0.014) on the final day of the fructan challenge compared to glucose.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: At the relatively high doses used, fructans, but not GOS or sorbitol, exacerbated FGS in patients with quiescent IBD, consistent with a re-challenge trial in irritable bowel syndrome. Further research is required to determine whether a low FODMAP diet reduces FGS in IBD and the degree of FODMAP restriction required for symptom improvement. Clinical trial registration number ISRCTN98226923.
